name: Interslavic constructed bridge
comprehension_evidence: Direct short written cloze evidence reports near 84 percent overall but is insufficient for sustained mathematical reading
production_architecture: Additional bridge edition alongside named natural-language editions; script-specific tests and overlap deductions
explicit_exclusions: Sorbian Kashubian Rusyn and every untested Slavic minority; no blanket Slavic coverage
notes: Only reviewed constructed bridge with substantial no-study evidence; local Open Logic surface is 7/722.

name: Romance semantic core and localized editions
proposed_surfaces: shared terminology graph plus Spanish Portuguese French Italian Romanian Catalan and other named localized outputs
comprehension_evidence: Natural-language intercomprehension and trainability are documented; no tested constructed pan-Romance surface
production_architecture: Common semantic source and cognate graph with named localized surfaces; optional intercomprehension apparatus
explicit_exclusions: No automatic coverage of Catalan Galician Occitan Sardinian Sicilian Neapolitan Friulian Romansh Ladin Aromanian Corsican or Judeo-Spanish
notes: The provisional local constructed surface has zero canon-admitted units and therefore zero bankable reach.

name: Turkic branch-level reuse
proposed_surfaces: separate Oghuz Kipchak and Karluk profiles with script-specific outputs
comprehension_evidence: Pairwise intelligibility is partial asymmetric and exposure-sensitive; no pan-Turkic surface is validated
production_architecture: Share semantics terminology and tooling within separately tested branches
explicit_exclusions: Chuvash Sakha Tuvan Khakas and other Oghur or Siberian languages; no one-surface family credit
notes: Complete Turkish edition is engineering and terminology evidence only.

name: Targeted Germanic reuse
proposed_surfaces: Dutch-Afrikaans first; separately test West and North residual profiles
comprehension_evidence: No functional evidence for a constructed pan-Germanic surface; Dutch-Afrikaans is the clearest narrower pair
production_architecture: Localized named editions with shared source and terminology where pairwise evidence supports reuse
explicit_exclusions: Yiddish Scots Low German Plautdietsch Pennsylvania Dutch Hutterisch Frisian Faroese and Icelandic are not covered by a pan-Germanic label
notes: High English overlap makes the family ceiling mostly irrelevant to marginal access.

name: Indonesian-Malaysian Malay package
proposed_surfaces: id-Latn-ID and ms-Latn-MY with optional locale-specific Jawi derivatives
comprehension_evidence: Strong relatedness and formal terminology coordination but documented lexical divergence; no whole technical-text comprehension test
production_architecture: One semantic and formula source with MABBIM-aligned termbase and explicit Indonesian and Malaysian layers
explicit_exclusions: Javanese Sundanese Madurese Minangkabau Acehnese and other Malayic or Indonesian languages are not covered
notes: Natural pluricentric case rather than a new constructed interlanguage.

name: Mainland Scandinavian localized package
comprehension_evidence: Strong but asymmetric natural intelligibility; Danish is harder; youth English overlap is extremely high
production_architecture: Share source terminology and layout but preserve named standards
explicit_exclusions: Faroese and Icelandic excluded; no blanket North Germanic coverage
notes: Likely compute savings but weak marginal-access case for a new bridge surface.

name: Modern Standard Arabic plus dialect scaffolds
proposed_surfaces: ar formal base plus region-specific term explanations audio and plain-language scaffolds
comprehension_evidence: MSA is an established formal bridge but accessibility varies with schooling and diglossic distance
production_architecture: Retain complete MSA edition; add dialect-aware scaffolding and accessible formats by region
explicit_exclusions: Amazigh Kurdish Nubian and Modern South Arabian languages; Arabic varieties are not assumed to be equally served
notes: Existing complete Arabic Open Logic edition changes this from new translation to residual-access work.

name: Persian-Dari-Tajik package
proposed_surfaces: fa-IR prs-Arab-AF tg-Cyrl-TJ with deterministic transliteration and localized terminology
comprehension_evidence: Formal varieties are close; script is a decisive barrier; transliteration is useful but directionally imperfect
production_architecture: Common semantic core with Iranian Persian Dari and Tajik lexical and script layers
explicit_exclusions: Kurdish Zazaki Pashto Balochi Ossetian Luri and Pamiri languages excluded
notes: Existing complete Iranian Persian edition makes Dari and Tajik adaptation the marginal intervention.

name: BCMS pluricentric package
comprehension_evidence: Very high mutual intelligibility with social national terminological and script distinctions
production_architecture: One common source with four explicitly named variants and Serbian dual-script rendering
explicit_exclusions: No unnamed neutral publication and no extension beyond the BCMS standards
notes: Strong compute-efficiency architecture with identity-preserving outputs.

name: Hindi-Urdu dual-register package
proposed_surfaces: hi-Deva-IN and ur-Arab-PK or ur-Arab-IN plus bilingual term graph
comprehension_evidence: Substantial everyday overlap but maximal divergence in script and advanced Sanskritic versus Persian-Arabic vocabulary
production_architecture: Shared syntax semantics and formula source with separate Devanagari and Nastaliq outputs and term layers
explicit_exclusions: India's 528347193 Hindi census umbrella is not Standard Hindi reach; no single technical Hindustani surface is credited
notes: Existing complete Hindi edition changes the marginal work to Urdu adaptation and equivalence tooling.

name: Punjabi two-script synchronized edition
comprehension_evidence: Same broad language continuum with two dominant scripts and regional terminology; no separate constructed surface required
production_architecture: Synchronized Gurmukhi and Shahmukhi outputs from a shared semantic and terminology source
explicit_exclusions: Saraiki Hindko and smaller Punjabi-associated census labels are not automatically included
notes: Census minimum combines India 2011 and Pakistan 2023 mother-tongue counts.

name: Nguni harmonized core with named standards
comprehension_evidence: High within-group intelligibility is reported but orthographic standards and false friends remain
production_architecture: Common semantic and terminology core with four named rendered standards
explicit_exclusions: No one isiZulu surface receives the combined population; non-Nguni South African languages excluded
notes: South African household shares provide a non-overlapping national ceiling before neighboring-country additions.

name: Sotho-Tswana harmonized core with named standards
proposed_surfaces: nso-Latn-ZA tn-Latn-ZA st-Latn-ZA and Botswana or Lesotho locale layers
comprehension_evidence: Close relationship supports reuse but written standards remain distinct
production_architecture: Common semantic and terminology core with named outputs
explicit_exclusions: Venda Tsonga and Nguni languages excluded
notes: South African household shares provide a lower national ceiling; Botswana and Lesotho require separate cells.

name: Manding plus N'Ko package
proposed_surfaces: Bamanan Maninka Jula named Latin outputs plus N'Ko literacy derivative
comprehension_evidence: A largely mutually intelligible continuum and an existing transnational N'Ko literary movement support a bridge hypothesis
production_architecture: Common semantic core with named national standards and Latin/N'Ko script outputs
explicit_exclusions: No blanket Mande-family coverage; exact communities and script literacy remain separate
notes: Jula 12.504 million is the only bounded numeric floor currently registered.

name: Southern Quechua shared core
proposed_surfaces: quy-Latn-PE quz-Latn-PE quh-Latn-BO and separately validated neighboring Southern profiles
comprehension_evidence: Southern varieties show meaningful intercomprehension; Northern and Central Quechua are more distant
production_architecture: Shared Southern semantic and terminology core with localized outputs
explicit_exclusions: Northern and Central Quechua excluded; Peru's aggregate is not awarded to one surface
notes: Peru's 2017 total is a ceiling until Southern shares and Bolivia counts are reconciled.
